sceneEssentials.label: Present-time action
sceneEssentials.question: What is happening that the camera and microphone can witness?
sceneEssentials.explanation: A scene unfolds through observable behavior or encounter. Background information may help the audience, but it is not a scene until something happens in time.

sceneEssentials.label: Specific place and time
sceneEssentials.question: Where and when does the event take place?
sceneEssentials.explanation: A scene has boundaries. Naming the location, time, and conditions makes the event filmable and helps the filmmaker anticipate image, sound, access, and change.

sceneEssentials.label: Contributor intention
sceneEssentials.question: What does the contributor want or need in this moment?
sceneEssentials.explanation: Intention gives action direction. It can be practical, emotional, relational, or uncertain, but it helps the audience understand why the moment matters.

sceneEssentials.label: Pressure or uncertainty
sceneEssentials.question: What could change, fail, be decided, or be discovered?
sceneEssentials.explanation: A scene needs possibility. The pressure may be quiet, but something must remain unresolved long enough for the audience to pay attention.

sceneEssentials.label: Visual and sound evidence
sceneEssentials.question: What can the audience see and hear for itself?
sceneEssentials.explanation: Documentary scenes make claims through evidence: behavior, objects, reactions, voices, spaces, rhythms, interruptions, and environmental sound.

sceneEssentials.label: Story consequence
sceneEssentials.question: What is different by the end of the scene?
sceneEssentials.explanation: A scene earns its place when it changes knowledge, feeling, relationship, direction, or stakes. The change may be small, but it should affect what comes next.

sceneTests.label: The station has served the neighborhood for thirty years.
sceneTests.explanation: This is useful background information, but no present-time event, contributor intention, or change is visible yet.

sceneTests.label: Maya sits at the radio console in the studio.
sceneTests.status: A setup—not yet a complete scene
sceneTests.explanation: The place and contributor are identifiable, but the action, pressure, and consequence still need to be defined.

sceneTests.label: Minutes before airtime, Maya and a volunteer trace a dead cable while the opening music continues to count down.
sceneTests.explanation: There is present-time action, a specific place and time, an intention, visible pressure, audiovisual evidence, and a possible change in outcome.

example.title: The Last Local Broadcast
example.subject: A volunteer-run community radio station facing the end of its lease.
example.contributor: Maya Alvarez, the host responsible for the station's final live program.
example.storyQuestion: Can Maya complete the last broadcast while deciding what the station's ending means for its listeners?

scenes.title: Preparing the final program
scenes.alt: Fictional community-radio host organizing notes and records before a broadcast
scenes.summary: Maya chooses music, arranges listener messages, and rehearses the opening in the nearly empty studio.
scenes.role: Establishes the contributor, ritual, place, and stakes.
scenes.turn: Preparation becomes emotionally difficult when Maya reaches the final listener message.
scenes.interview: Static interview after preparation: Maya explains what the station has meant to her.

scenes.title: The signal chain fails
scenes.alt: Fictional radio host and volunteer producer checking a cable at the studio console
scenes.summary: A microphone channel fails shortly before airtime, forcing Maya and a volunteer to diagnose the problem.
scenes.role: Introduces pressure and makes the broadcast uncertain.
scenes.turn: Maya abandons the planned setup and chooses a simpler backup microphone.
scenes.interview: Dynamic interview during the repair: short questions reveal the decision without stopping the action.

scenes.title: The final live hour
scenes.alt: Fictional community-radio host speaking live while a volunteer producer monitors equipment
scenes.summary: Maya broadcasts listener messages while the volunteer monitors the repaired signal.
scenes.role: Delivers the central encounter and tests whether the plan can hold.
scenes.turn: A caller changes Maya's prepared ending and she responds live.
scenes.interview: No formal interview: the broadcast and reactions are the primary scene evidence.

scenes.title: After the transmitter goes quiet
scenes.alt: Fictional radio host alone in the studio after the final broadcast
scenes.summary: Maya removes her headphones, saves the recording, and walks through the silent studio.
scenes.role: Shows consequence and gives the story a changed emotional state.
scenes.turn: Maya decides to preserve the final program as the beginning of a community archive.
scenes.interview: Static interview in the silent studio: reflection follows observable aftermath.
